title: MFMNet: Adaptive tri-layer graph pyramid with cross-scale attention router for synergistic drug prediction
content:
by Lei Wang, Liping Sun, Jingwen Pan, Guangming Shao, Guokun Shi, Guanyu Zhang, Yucheng Shi, Li Jin

Background and objective

Experimental screening of synergistic anticancer drug pairs is time-consuming, while effectively integrating complementary molecular graph representations with cell-line-specific information remains challenging for computational drug-synergy prediction.

Methods

We developed MFMNet with a Tri-Layer Graph Pyramid (TGP) comprising GCN, GIN, and GAT branches for extracting complementary molecular graph representations. A Cross-Scale Attention Router (CSAR), implemented as an adaptive feature-wise gating mechanism, integrates the graph representations before they are combined with drug embeddings and cell-line transcriptomic features for synergistic drug-pair prediction.

Results

In the initial five-fold cross-validation analysis, MFMNet achieved a mean five-fold AUROC of 0.9301 ± 0.0036. Under the stricter fold-matched evaluation protocol, the full MFMNet backbone achieved an AUROC of 0.9227 ± 0.0055 and a PR-AUC of 0.9127 ± 0.0084, with statistically significant improvements over XGBoost, DeepDDS-GCN, and DeepDDS-GAT after Holm correction.

Conclusions

MFMNet provides a computational framework for synergistic drug-pair prediction by integrating complementary molecular graph representations with drug and cell-line features. The results support its use for computational prioritization of candidate synergistic drug combinations. All reported performance estimates refer to record-level five-fold cross-validation within the O'Neil dataset; generalization to entirely unseen drugs and cell lines requires further study.
author: Lei Wang
